_readme: Every place in the production trees that runs an ARBITRARY command (a shell command string)
or replaces the process image with an arbitrary argv. Fixed-argv spawns (git, rg, uname) are
not listed: their argv is decided by us, not by the turn, so a kernel boundary adds nothing.
status 'confined'    -> hermes_acl.policy.wrap_argv is applied, so the kernel confines the
child (filesystem roots, no network) when acl.enabled=true.
status 'out-of-scope'-> deliberately outside the boundary. The reason MUST say why; a
reviewer has to be able to disagree with it.
Keyed by file with spawn_sites = the number of sites the scanner finds there. A count is
stable under line drift and changes exactly when someone adds or removes a command site —
the event this inventory exists to catch. Update it DELIBERATELY: if the new child is not
confined, the entry's status and reason are what make that visible in review.

files.reason: /bin/sh -c <operator's secret-command from config> with a hard 3 s timeout, to mint a credential. The command is written by the host owner in config.yaml about their own machine; there is no second subject whose files it could reach.

Shutdown forensics: a FIXED script we ship, run while the gateway dies to flush a dump to a log the owner reads. Nothing from a turn; bounding it with Landlock would also deny it the /proc and /sys reads it exists to collect.

Builds 'sh -lc <command>' to open a terminal WINDOW on the owner's desktop (xterm/gnome-terminal). The launcher execs a terminal EMULATOR, so a shim on this argv would confine the emulator and the shell inside it would inherit the emulator's own process, not the shim's. Recorded as a residual gap: the desktop launcher is not confined.

Runs a FIXED stop script (pid + start time as arguments) as a DIFFERENT USER in the sandbox namespace via streams.run_in. The isolation there is the user+namespace boundary, which the shim cannot cross anyway (a different uid cannot be confined by our ruleset file).
THE foreground terminal path (_run_bash). The argv builder at 1159 is wrapped at 1166 before Popen at 1169; this is the boundary the whole task is about.

_scope_argv builds the login-shell argv and wraps it with wrap_argv before the pipe/PTY spawn (spawn_local -> _spawn_job / PtyProcessCls.spawn). The scanner reports the builder, not the spawn, because the argv reaches _spawn_job as a parameter.

'bash <launcher script>' with a FIXED script path and no command string from the turn; the launcher is a program we ship. Confining it would also kill the per-profile screen it exists to keep alive after its starter dies (start_new_session).

spawn_owned(<operator-configured TTS command>, shell=True) — the command comes from config.yaml, written by the host OWNER about their own machine, not from a turn. It runs in the owner's own profile with the owner's own files; there is no second subject to isolate.

Runs a SKILL's install/verify command. A skill is operator- or library-supplied code with full Python access to the same process — confining only its shell helper would imply an isolation that the surrounding skill execution does not provide. Named in ACCEPTED-RISKS instead.
Mints a credential via the operator's own configured token command (config.yaml, owner scope). Same reasoning as tts_command_provider: the owner's own helper, no second subject.

Runs an INBOUND HOOK: operator-written shell in config for a messaging event, with a 30 s bound. Owner configuration, not a turn. Confining it is conceivable but the hook's contract is 'run this on my host as me'.

Runs a session's configured init/warm-up shell ONCE at session creation from the session record, not from a turn. Listed for review: if that record becomes turn-influenced, this becomes a confined site.
'!cmd' typed by the HUMAN at the CLI prompt — the human is the owner of the machine, running in their own terminal with their own privileges. There is no boundary to draw against themselves.
Gate command from the operator's goal definition in config; owner scope, no second subject.
Catalog BOOTSTRAP commands run by an explicit `hermes mcp add` on the owner's own machine, with the catalog's own scripts. Owner-scope install action.
Slash-command shell for the TUI host process: the owner's own interactive surface, same reasoning as bang_shell. Its tool calls reach the agent's terminal path, which IS confined.

os.execv re-exec of the SAME interpreter during early-recovery (before any config or session exists, so no acl policy can be loaded yet). Replacing the image cannot be wrapped: a shim would exec and the parent would be gone.
os.execvp('sleep', ['sleep','infinity']) — a container keep-alive with a fixed argv. Nothing from a turn; also the last statement of a boot path.

os.execvp into a container runtime (docker exec ...). The isolation boundary there is the CONTAINER, which is strictly stronger than Landlock; adding a shim would confine the client, not the workload.
os.execvpe re-exec of this same process for CPU profiling (argv built by us, fixed). Nothing from a turn.
os.execvp re-exec of this same program after an update; argv is ours. Replacing the image cannot be wrapped.
